_comment:
config.json -- input to solenoid3d.py.

    Layout:
      experiment  : global experiment metadata
      physics     : shared physics (gravity, mass, air drag, magnet properties)
      mesh        : mesh sizes
      geometry    : air-domain extents
      curves      : LIST of curve blocks, ONE per body geometry. To add a new
                    curve, simply add another named entry under [curves]. Each
                    block must carry:  label, color, z_release_m, N_turns,
                    R_load_ohm, damping_extra_N_s_per_m, body_name, sif_suffix.
                    Wire-related keys (wire_diameter_m,
                    wire_conductivity_S_per_m) are read when N_turns > 0.

experiment.name: magnet_free_fall
experiment.description: Permanent cylindrical magnet released from rest above the coil. We track trajectory, flux, EMF, induced current and the Lenz braking force for multiple coil configurations.

coil._comment: Coil/bore body geometry as built by solenoid3d.py (S_IN/S_OUT/S_Z0/S_Z1). Used by the oscilloscope to integrate the flux through the winding.

mesh._comment: Sizes are applied to the corner POINTS of each volume (required with General.ExpertMode=1). The magnet and coil are refined locally; the far-field air stays coarse. The TRANSIENT run performs one direct linear solve per timestep, so the total node count directly drives wall-clock time.

empty._comment: REFERENCE -- no conductor at all. Free-fall baseline (no Lenz braking, no induced current).
empty.label: 空 (无导体)

copper_closed._comment: 铜线闭路 CLOSED CIRCUIT, copper. 50 turns of 0.7 mm Cu wire (sigma=5.96e7) into a 10 ohm load. Current flows -> EMF/R, Lenz braking and Joule loss.
copper_closed.label: 铜线闭路 (Cu 50t 0.7mm, R=10Ω)

aluminum_closed._comment: 铝线闭路 CLOSED CIRCUIT, aluminium. Same 50 turns / 0.7 mm but sigma=3.5e7, so R_wire is 1.70x the copper value (0.527 vs 0.310 ohm) into the same 10 ohm load.
aluminum_closed.label: 铝线闭路 (Al 50t 0.7mm, R=10Ω)

aluminum_open._comment: 铝线开路 OPEN CIRCUIT, aluminium. Same winding but R_load=inf: the EMF still appears across the terminals, I = 0, therefore NO Lenz braking. Compare against aluminum_closed to isolate the circuit-state effect.
aluminum_open.label: 铝线开路 (Al 50t 0.7mm, R=∞)
